summary: 1942 U.S. Army sentry and fire lookout on Picatinny Arsenal, Morris County; NHLR-registered 1994, closed to the public since 2001, slated for demolition in 2020.

facts.design: 60-foot steel Aeromotor LS-40 tower with a catwalk around the cab
facts.status_note: Standing in the newest source found, a September 2023 Register visit report. The cab is deteriorating, and the tower was slated for demolition in 2020.

access.note: Public access closed since 2001, per the Register's 2020 visit report. The site is run by Picatinny Arsenal.

visit.trail_note: No public visits. The tower sits inside Picatinny Arsenal, and access has been closed since 2001. Ask Picatinny before going near it.

events.note: Built by the U.S. Army as a sentry and fire-detection site overlooking the explosive assembly area
April 1994 forest fire stopped with a backfire at the tower
Cab restored in 1994; the two sources disagree on who did the work and whether it is complete
Public access closed since 2001, per the 2020 Register visit report
Abandoned for use as a radio tower and sits dormant, per the August 2020 visit report
Slated for demolition; the New Jersey Forest Fire Service expressed interest in taking it over
Cab lit for the first time in nearly 30 years, September 5, 2020, during the Lighting of the Fire Towers
September 2023 visit: cab deteriorated further; not likely to last more than five years at that rate

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: the 1994 NHLR registration is correct. No corrections needed. Access was 'unknown' and is now 'closed', per the NHLR 2020 visit report. Sources disagree on the 1994 cab restoration: the NHLR description (undated) says it is complete and the NJ FFLA chapter took on the rebuild; the Army article credits the NHLR volunteers and says the cab has since decayed. The newest source is the September 2023 visit report, so current condition and whether the 2020 demolition plan went ahead are unconfirmed. Wikipedia's 380 m elevation differs slightly from NHLR's 378 m; the story does not use either. No new photos recorded (no image URLs read).
